decision: Illustrative order quantities for all 336 supplied keys; operations inputs are explicitly synthetic.
target: Positive non-cancelled recorded ordered product units by order date, all sales channels assigned to their supplied store. Normalize status case/whitespace, remove exact full-row duplicates, retain positive returned/return-flagged and processing orders. Exclude zero/negative quantities; do not infer usable return stock.
status_information_limit: Only supplied final statuses available, no status-change timestamps; historical simulations are conditional on these statuses, not a reconstruction of what was known then.
population: Fixed 336 keys from supplied policy/inventory, equal key/origin weights; current supplied assortment used retrospectively, with future-population knowledge disclosed. Check actual first appearance before comparisons.
missing_dates: After first appearance assume complete extract: absence means zero recorded orders, not proven zero demand. Before first appearance unknown, not zero; calendar exposure starts at first appearance. Test alternative observed-active-day denominators as exploratory sensitivity only, not an alternative verified truth. Check missing network dates and sparse key-days.
training: Strictly before each origin; local windows 28/91/182/364 calendar days. Seasonal factors use completed years before origin year only. No December sales access.
primary_horizon: Seven-day total starting at origin, all 336 keys and all scheduled origins.
secondary_coverage_horizon: Current supplied lead time plus 7-day review (8-14 days), illustrative historical diagnostic using current policy, not historical policy. Score only key/origins whose entire horizon ends by 2025-11-30; identical subset for all candidates. It cannot override primary selection. Deployment uses this coverage horizon, a disclosed mismatch.
baseline: Local trailing 91-calendar-day daily mean times horizon. Analytical interpretation of recent months, not an exact replica of the customer's unspecified buying rule.
shared: Daily rate = 0.5*local trailing364 daily mean + 0.5*network trailing91 daily rate * trailing364 product unit share * trailing364 store unit share. Shares computed from all eligible network units before origin.
seasonal: Shared daily rate multiplied for each future day by its month factor / mean month factor over trailing91 calendar days. Factors: mean network daily units for each month across completed years before origin year, normalized by unweighted mean of 12 monthly means. No factors from origin year or future records.
primary_metric: MAE of seven-day total, product units per key/week; arithmetic mean absolute error with equal key/origin weight. Recorded-unit forecast error, not availability, purchasing cost or savings.
selection: Select smallest initial-period primary MAE; numerical ties within 1e-12 prefer baseline then local28, local182, local364, shared, seasonal. Retain baseline unless that same initial winner reduces MAE >=5% versus baseline in BOTH development periods. Do not promote another candidate from diagnostics. This 5% is a supplied engineering stability rule, not commercial value or externally declared success threshold.
secondary_diagnostics: seasonal factor stability by prior year
development residual spread and order sensitivity
readiness: Both periods are development, October-November previously inspected. No untouched evaluation or savings claim; recording readiness remains unestablished and needs external meaningful threshold and frozen artifacts evaluated on genuinely untouched outcomes. Reserved December outcomes remain untouched.
order_rule: End-of-Nov30 stock available at start Dec1 assumed. Cover expected recorded units from Dec1 over lead+review plus supplied safety stock. Subtract usable stock and only inbound due within coverage; avoid double counting on-order aggregate. Round positive shortfall up to supplied minimum and order multiple. Flag expected shortages before new order arrival; retain zero orders where covered. No budget/shelf/service-cost optimization without inputs. Sensitivity columns are scenarios, not confidence bounds.
